content:
**Key observations:**
- Sugarcane plant at/near soil level, showing complete leaf bleaching (straw-white color)
- Leaves have lost all green pigment — uniformly pale/cream/straw-colored
- Dark discoloration visible at the crown/base where stem meets soil
- Plant appears to be dying from the base upward
- No discrete spots or mosaic patterns visible

**Reasoning through classes:**
- **Brown_Spot / Yellow_Spot**: Would show discrete lesions, not uniform bleaching
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv / Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Would show mosaic/streak patterns, still with some green
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Yellowing of midrib, not full-leaf straw bleaching
- **Grassy_Shoot**: Excessive thin grass-like tillers — not present here
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Twisted/distorted spindle leaves — not evident
- **Sett_Rot**: Rotting of the planted sett at soil level, killing the plant before establishment — the dark rotted crown and completely desiccated leaves dying from the base up fits well
- **Leaf_Scald**: Uniform cream/white bleaching of the entire leaf blade ("scalded" appearance), can progress to top-rot and plant death

The uniform, complete straw-white bleaching of the entire leaf surface running lengthwise (not spotty, not mosaic) along with the dying plant from the crown is most characteristic of **Leaf Scald** in its severe "scalded" phase, caused by *Xanthomonas albilineans*.
